title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Frobenius-class-folded distinguished-point rho in GT

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity P in G1 and independent uniform z in GT (identity included), the sequential classical algorithm of proof.md returns Q in G2 with e(P,Q)=z with probability at least 0.39 over (P,z) and the algorithm's coins, using at most 2^125.90 total target-group-operation equivalents (dense Fp12 multiplication = 1, C = 20,000), including every table construction, pairing, start, step, probe, report, store operation, replay, verification and output step. The algorithm sets g = e(P,Q0), solves z = g^a by a distinguished-point rho walk on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT (x ~ x^p, which acts as x -> x^lambda with lambda = p mod r of order 12) and outputs Q = [a]Q0. The class walk uses a 4-multiplication Frobenius-covariant selector, an R = 2^14 table of twisted multipliers, a 24-class look-back window held as a sorted array with deterministic probing, distinguished-point density 2^-80, trail cap 2^87, and exponent recovery by replaying the two colliding trails. Each multiplication slot is charged 1 + 2900/20000 units: 2,900 instructions itemised in proof.md section 5 as 2,865 of hard per-item bounds plus a 1.2% margin. The accepted-step budget is S_max = ceil(sqrt(2*mu*N*ln(1000/608))) with N = (r-1)/12 classes and mu = 11/10, giving total work at most 2^125.89684 (the claim rounds up to 2^125.90, proved directly by the exact integer inequalities W^100 <= 2^12590 and W^100 > 2^12589 on the exact rational total W). Preprocessing is at most 2^24.13 units and is included in the total; nonuniform advice is none (0 bytes); peak memory is at most 2^54 bytes (at most 2^47 store records of 96 bytes, a 113 MB twist table and under 2^20 bytes of state), all within one 2^64-byte address space. Success is a heuristic claim and rests on disclosed hypotheses: H1 (random-mapping birthday behaviour of the class walk with walk-quality loss at most mu = 11/10 and negligible coalescence loss), H2 (pseudorandomness of the hash fields h and the distinguished-point predicate derived from the class key, and iid uniform twist offsets for distinct classes), H3 (ideal algorithm coins). Under H1-H3 the main-event probability is at least 392/1000 at S_max and all other losses (stated in proof.md section 6) are below 0.001, so the success probability is at least 0.3917 > 0.39. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice and no quantum steps; it is an analytic claim, not a production-scale execution.

experiments.purpose: One bounded run of four parts, none of which is a production-scale run. (1) ledger: recompute the exact work ledger of proof.md section 5 (S_max, M_max, the itemised per-slot instructions, the additive items, log2 W_max <= claim with the exact integer check W^100 <= 2^12590), the memory ledger and the trap-lemma bound of section 7 (arithmetic on the stated prices only, no instruction counts measured). (2) algebra: on real BLS12-381 GT elements check lambda = p mod r has order 12 with lambda^6 = -1, Frobenius equals x -> x^lambda, the 12 selector candidates equal the true first coordinates of c1(sigma^k(y)), the class key is Frobenius invariant, k* is covariant, and the twisted walk step is class-equivariant. (3) toy: run the complete algorithm (selector, twisted table, look-back window with probing, distinguished points, store, replay with exponent tracking, Frobenius alignment, g^a == z) over a toy tower of the production shape with real Fp12 arithmetic and a 22-23 bit subgroup, checking recovered logarithms and that tracked replays reproduce the untracked paths. (4) sim: exponent-domain emulation of the identical walk with the production table size, measuring the walk-quality constant mu_hat at the first inter-trail class repeat against an ideal value 1 and a plain-birthday control, the fraction of groups whose first repeat falls inside the S_max budget (the statistic the claim uses; ideal map 0.4215, required 0.3903), the escape rate against 1/(12R), and whether meeting trails reach the same distinguished point. Toy sizes only; extrapolation to production is a disclosed heuristic (proof.md sections 6 and 9).
